records.query: Explain the components and design of the AFTF.
records.reference: The AFTF (Aircraft Fire Training Facility) is a fixed site simulator for realistic aircraft fire suppression training. It includes a 100-foot burn area, an aircraft mock-up with water-cooled jackets and ignitors, a water pond, and a 10,000-gallon tank for water recycling. The fuel system uses liquid propane (LPG) to simulate multiple fire types, including airframe, engine, and ground fires. The facility is managed via a safety/control stand with electrical, pneumatic, and water systems, and is equipped with manual/pneumatic shutoff valves, an E-stop switch, and fuel shutoff valves for JP-8 and propane for emergency control.
records.answer:
The Air Force Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) is a generic, adaptable site design. It consists of an aircraft mock-up, a lined burn area with underground liner, a control stand, a compressor shelter, and integrated systems: liquid propane fuel, cathodic (anti-corrosion) protection, pneumatic, electrical, and a water conservation system with a holding pond incorporating submerged and aeration pumps, sprinkler, water jackets, and drain and wash-down systems.

Configuration: A 100-foot (30-meter) lined burn area with an aircraft mock-up and a 10,000 water gallon (38,000 liter) liquid propane tank provides live fires to simulate multi-aircraft fires. Propane is supplied through underground pipes, and fuel is ignited by 10,000 volt, 23 milliampere ignitors in 15 burners. Switches and valves on the control stand control fires during training. The fully lined facility protects the environment from ground water contamination.

Aircraft mock-up: Uncoated/unpainted carbon steel, approximately 72 feet long, 25 feet high at tail tip, with a 72-foot wingspan. It has four simulated engines, each with a burner assembly and two ignitors, with ignitor wiring enclosed in water jackets. Water injection is in the wing engines and at some sites in the tail engine. A water sprinkler along the fuselage top cools and washes down the mock-up. An expansion joint at mid-fuselage allows for expansion and contraction. Replaceable 0.031 inch sheet metal cutout panels on each side simulate emergency entry.

Consumables: Solenoids, regulators, valves, switches, and ignitors are to be discarded upon disassembly unless manufacturer-authorized rebuild/repair kits are available.

Variants: Site configurations may vary depending on component use and on-site location. The Edwards AFB site is partially locally manufactured and partially ICS designed. The design has been revised over time, from CFRTF-3 (1991) through AFTF-P-4.1 (2013). Maintenance is performed by Civil Engineering or contractor personnel.

records.query: Summarize the procedures and safety requirements for removing, packaging, and handling wet and dry batteries from vehicles; mention hazard precautions as well.
records.reference: Wet batteries (except nickel, iron-alkaline) must be removed from vehicles and reported as excess, kept charged, and maintained in a charged condition while awaiting disposal instructions. Dry batteries should be space packaged and packed in accordance with Specification PPP-B-140, with vent holes sealed. Battery posts must be protected using plastic caps or tape conforming to Specification SAE AMS-T-22085. Wet batteries may remain installed in vehicles during military aircraft transport if protected against short circuits by disconnecting and securing cables away from terminals, and properly secured to prevent acid leakage. Dry batteries pose no special hazard and may be installed in the vehicle or shipped with OVE without additional precautions. Wet batteries received with vehicles may be used until the first exercise is completed, after which they must be transferred to a battery room, kept charged, and either shipped or replaced with dry batteries. Dry batteries, whether received charged or not, can be stored in the vehicle’s battery carrier, though indoor storage is preferred, and their vent holes must be sealed until activation. Cable terminals should be greased and taped according to military specifications, and dry batteries must not be activated unless no serviceable wet battery is available. Hazard precautions include preventing acid leakage and short circuits for wet batteries, and ensuring proper handling and activation procedures for dry batteries to avoid chemical exposure.
records.answer:
Summary (TO 36-1-191, vehicle processing for storage/shipment):

Wet batteries (removal and handling):
- Wet batteries removed from vehicles are reported to the appropriate property class as excess, requesting disposition instructions, and must be maintained in a charged condition while awaiting disposition.
- Lead-acid wet batteries may remain in the vehicle for Level B/C conditions, or for exercise purposes under Level A outdoor storage until no longer capable of recharging. Disconnect cables, move cable ends away from posts, and cover posts with plastic caps or tape (electric tape excluded per AMS-T-22085).
- Batteries remaining in vehicles are secured in the battery box and kept fully charged. Shrouding is optional at the discretion of the responsible officer.
- Electrolyte is packaged and packed per O-S-801 and stowed with other OVE, in a manner permitting easy removal at ports when maritime regulations require it.
- Nickel-iron-alkaline batteries: confirm electrolyte is at the recommended level and filler caps are closed; discharge at normal rate to 0.5 V per cell; short-circuit each tray leaving wires connected. They may be received discharged, dumped of electrolyte and short-circuited; electrolyte (potassium and lithium hydroxide in water) is packaged as specified and identified to the battery type.

Dry batteries:
- Secure in vehicle battery carriers; plug or seal filler cap vent holes; package and pack per Specification PPP-B-140.

Air shipment:
- Wet batteries may be airlifted installed only if completely protected against short circuits (cables removed, ends secured away from terminals) and secured so acid leakage will not occur. Dry batteries present no special hazard and may stay in the carrier or be placed with OVE. Battery acid is packed per AFMAN 24-204(1P) and attached to the vehicle under the hood for air or sea shipment.

Hazard precautions:
- WARNING: Electrolyte is highly toxic to skin, eyes and respiratory tract. Avoid all contact. Skin and eye protection and vapor control are required. Have the operation reviewed by the local Bioenvironmental Engineer. Failure to comply could result in injury to, or death of, personnel or long-term health hazards.
- Battery compartment coatings: use acid- and alkali-resistant coating to resist sulfuric acid and potassium hydroxide. Lacquer, sealant and polyurethane paint are flammable and toxic; observe ventilation, ignition-source and respirator requirements as stated on the page.
- WARNING (drive belt primer, TT-P-664): toxic to skin, eyes and respiratory tract; use with adequate ventilation, respirator in enclosed areas without ventilation, and goggles or face shield, gloves, apron.
- Remove batteries from NMCS vehicles only when climatic conditions or security concerns warrant; identify them with the vehicle registration number and store in an appropriate location.
- Hazardous materials for air shipment must be classified and certified per AFMAN 24-204(1P); hazardous materials are not to be stripped for airlift.

Note: The pages do not state electrolyte spill cleanup procedures, and do not give a separate step-by-step removal procedure for every battery type.

The candidate covers (1), (2), (3) roughly, (4) and (5). It does give hazard precautions, but these are extra, such as electrolyte toxicity, and it does not clearly state the activation chemical exposure precautions. Several key facts are missing or different, so the answer fails.

records.query: List the processes in included in the Equipment Painting and list the precautions to be considered during surface painting.
records.reference: Equipment painting includes cleaning surfaces with degreasing solvents (MIL-PRF-680, Type II) and isopropyl alcohol (TT-I-735) to remove oil, grease, rust, and dirt; sanding glossy areas and removing rust by wire brushing; priming bare spots; and applying two coats of paint, allowing each coat to dry. Precautions include using PPE (eye, skin, and respiratory protection), ensuring adequate ventilation, avoiding contact with flammable and hazardous chemicals, following OSHA safety color coding, and not painting transparent shields. Items must be painted with materials that are not affected by fluids or cleaning solutions used in the machines.
records.answer:
The pages do not contain a section titled "Equipment Painting." The closest matches are TO 36-1-191 (vehicle and equipment painting, Chapter 2) and TO 1-1-8 Chapters 3 through 5 (surface preparation and painting operations for aircraft and equipment).

PROCESSES: Thermal spray equipment (MWAS process and metalized coatings) (TO 36-1-191); two-part primer system of zinc-rich primer conforming to MIL-PRF-26915 Type II plus MIL-DTL-53030 intermediate primer applied wet-to-wet; ceramic-loaded epoxy coatings and spray-in bed liners (aliphatic polyurea); spray application methods including HVLP, hot, airless, air-assisted airless and electrostatic spray (TO 1-1-8); preparation for painting, including draining and steaming of fuel servicing trucks and trailer tanks with a grounded conductive steam hose.

PRECAUTIONS DURING SURFACE PREPARATION AND PAINTING: Surface preparation is the most important requirement for ensuring proper adherence and performance of a paint system. Refer to Table 3-1 for minimum PPE for all paint preparation operations, and provide adequate ventilation when using solvents while avoiding prolonged breathing of vapors and skin contact. Metalizing produces high noise levels, metal oxide fumes and ultraviolet radiation; consult the bioenvironmental engineer for PPE. Surfaces with visible moisture, rust, scale or contamination must be re-blasted or mechanically cleaned before metalizing and coated within six hours of abrasive blasting. Metalized coating is applied to 6 to 8 mils. Zinc-rich primer is designed only for properly prepared bare steel and must not be used as an intercoat adhesion promoter for topcoat touch-up; follow the primer manufacturer's guidance on spray gun and fluid tip selection to avoid clogging. If 24 hours elapse between priming and topcoating, solvent wipe reactivation is not permitted and scuff sanding is mandatory. Coatings and thinners contain toxic substances, so wear approved respiratory protection and protective clothing, and spray only in areas approved by Fire, Safety and Bioenvironmental Engineering. Paint spray respirators meeting NIOSH requirements must be worn during spray operations. Indoor spray painting requires a paint spray room with a minimum face air velocity of 125 feet per minute. Smoking and open flame devices are prohibited in the paint shop, and dirty rags must be kept in metal self-closing containers and removed at the end of each shift. For electrostatic painting of fueled aircraft, on-board JP-8 fuel must be below 100°F (38°C) before and during painting, the aircraft must be grounded in two locations, exhaust must be kept below 20 percent of LEL with no more than 500 PPM total solvent vapor, and the fire suppression system must be fully operational before painting starts.

records.query: What are the procedures for installing, removing, and requisitioning vehicle markings, including reflective tape?
records.reference: Vehicle markings, including reflective tape, are installed by cleaning the surface, removing the liner, positioning the tape, and applying firm pressure. For removal, pressure-sensitive tape can be softened with heat and isopropyl alcohol (TT-I-735), while older tape requires paint remover (TT-R-2918) or 3M decal remover disks. Markings can be requisitioned through DLA Document Services Online. If decals are unavailable and safety is impacted, stenciling is permitted. Reflectors follow drawing B161059, mounted 24–60 inches above the ground, visible at 100 feet. Install tape according to the steps; damaged areas may be patched.
records.answer:
Source: TO 36-1-191 (vehicle markings).

INSTALLATION of reflectorized tape (para 2.88):
a. Clean the vehicle surface before applying the marking.
b. Remove the liner film down.
c. Position the emblem on the clean surface and tack it in place with thumb pressure.
d. Start in the center and use hard overlapping strokes of low-friction plastic squeeze.
e. Re-squeeze the edges using very firm strokes.
f. Apply clean sealer to the edges of the tape.
g. Repairs to damaged areas can be made without stripping the original tape: clean the damaged area and apply new tape over the affected area.

REMOVAL of reflectorized tape (para 2.89):
WARNING: Lacquer thinner, kylol, and isopropyl alcohol are flammable and toxic. Good general ventilation is normally adequate. Skin and eye protection is required. Avoid all sources of ignition. Failure to comply could result in injury to, or death of, personnel or long-term health hazards.
- Routine removal (2.89.1): Soften the pressure-sensitive tape with heat (heat lamp, heat gun, steam, etc.); soften adhesive residue with rags soaked in isopropyl alcohol, TT-1-735, and scrape away with a plastic scraper or putty knife.
- Removing old tape (2.89.2): If tape has been on for several years, mask off the surrounding area and brush paint remover, TT-R-2918, Type over the tape. Several applications may be needed at short intervals; remove residue with a plastic scraper or bevel-edge putty knife between applications. Paint remover may damage the underlying paint, requiring cleaning and touch-up painting.
- Alternative (2.89.3): Use a 4 or 6 inch stripe, molding and decal remover disk (3M), NSN 5130-01-390-9503 (4 inch) or 5130-01-390-9504 (6 inch), with adapter NSN 5130-01-391-2095 for a drill. This removes tape without damaging the paint.
NOTE: The solvents are flammable and toxic; take all safety precautions.

WAR RESERVE MATERIEL (WRM) triangle (para 2.87): When a vehicle is removed from WRM status, the triangle must be removed. WRM markings should not be removed when a WRM asset is shipped to a contingency area.

REQUISITIONING (para 2.90): All markings in the chapter are requisitioned through DLA Document Services. Submit requests via the Document Services Online (DSO) website; once an account is created, orders are processed through the Travis Plant. DLA Document Services: (707) 424-0770 / (707) 424-4537, DSN 837.
NOTE: If decals are not immediately available and the unmarked equipment hampers mission capability or presents a safety hazard, markings may be stenciled on the vehicle or equipment before decals are received.

Limitation: The pages I read do not include the full marking specifications or the complete reflective tape stock list, and the WARNING text at the end of para 2.89 is truncated in the source.

records.query: What caution is taken into consideration while using high-pressure wash equipment, and explain the function of the portable, 45-gallon, foam-generating cleaning unit?
records.reference: When using high-pressure wash equipment, caution must be taken to ensure it is never used on aircraft landing gear and components, wheels, and brakes, as it can force lubricants out of bearings and attachment points, causing corrosion and wear problems. The function of the portable, 45-gallon, foam-generating cleaning unit is to dispense foam. This cleaning unit is a simplified, portable, pressure-operated, foam-dispensing system that uses the available air supply as its power source to force cleaning solution into the hose and create foam.
records.answer:
Caution with high-pressure wash equipment:
- Equipment developing more than 175 PSI nozzle pressure must not be used to apply cleaning compounds unless specifically authorized by the equipment System Program Manager (SPM); otherwise damage to or destruction of equipment or loss of mission effectiveness may result (TO 1-1-700). The pages read do not state that cleaning compounds should be applied only with a low-pressure soap nozzle.
- High-pressure wash equipment must never be used on components, wheels, and brakes, as it can force lubricants out of bearings and attach points and cause corrosion and wear (TO 35-1-3).
- If approved by the SPM, use only 40-degree flat fan spray nozzles, keep nozzle standoff at least 12 inches from the surface, and use a 50:50 water-to-cleaner mix. High-pressure cleaning may remove loose sealant and/or paint (TO 1-1-700).

Portable 45-gallon foam-generating cleaning unit function:
It is a simplified, portable, pressure-operated foam-dispensing system. It uses the available air supply as its power source without pumps: air is metered directly into the pressurized solution chamber, which forces cleaning solution into the hose to create foam. The operator adjusts the cleaning compound metering valve and air pressure (30 to 70 PSI at the regulator) to set foam wetness. The foam is applied to the surface, allowed to dwell for at least one minute without drying, then scrubbed with a cleaning kit, brush, or cloth and rinsed. Wet foam cleans better; dry foam prolongs dwell time. The unit has a 45-gallon stainless steel tank and 50 ft of 5/8-in ID foaming hose.

Safety: WARNING – do not service the unit without releasing tank pressure (close the metering and air valves and open the air dump valve to bleed retained air). CAUTION – after use, drain and flush the tank with fresh water to avoid an extremely concentrated solution that could damage the equipment being cleaned.

records.query: Define CSO and list down the activities performed in the presence of CSS.
records.reference: Concurrent Servicing Operations (CSO) are the simultaneous servicing of fuel and other aircraft operations such as munitions loading/unloading, aircraft reconfiguration, and aircraft -6 TO inspections. The Chief Servicing Supervisor (CSS) is responsible for on-site supervision of all aspects of concurrent fuel servicing operations. The CSS's activities include ensuring all non-essential personnel and equipment are cleared from the area, briefing team members on duties and emergency procedures, checking the status of the aircraft and its systems with the SCR, ensuring cabin crew have briefed passengers, directing and monitoring the positioning of support equipment and personnel, and having SPR/Vent monitors reposition aircraft wheel chocks as required.
records.answer:
CSO (Concurrent Servicing Operations) supporting Combat Sortie Generation (CSG) is the simultaneous fueling and munitions/ammunition loading/unloading, aircraft reconfiguration, aircraft -6 TO inspections, and other aircraft servicing such as oil, nitrogen, and hydraulic fluid. Oxygen servicing is not accomplished during fuel servicing. (CSO supporting CSG from release 27 is now known as ICT; servicing with no munitions loading/unloading or aircraft reconfiguration is just "Concurrent Servicing.")

Activities performed in the presence of a CSS: The key function requiring a CSS is refueling/defueling. A CSS is required when fuel servicing is performed simultaneously with:
1. Aircraft -6 and -6WC inspections
2. Munitions/ammunition loading/unloading
3. Aircraft reconfiguration
4. Other aircraft servicing such as oil, nitrogen, and hydraulic fluid

Note: Electrical "power-on" portions of -6 inspections are not authorized during concurrent munitions loading/unloading and fuel servicing; they are accomplished before or after the concurrent operation.

Not requiring a CSS: When no refuel/defuel is taking place, a CSS is not required for munitions loading/unloading, aircraft -6/-6WC inspections, reconfiguration, or oil/nitrogen/hydraulic servicing (the weapons load crew chief controls those actions). A CSS is not used during ICTs; an Aircraft Turnaround Supervisor (ATS) is used instead and must be present for the entire ICT.

records.query: Outline the exception for taxiing within the 50-foot hot refueling safety zone, specifying the engine boundary rule and the mandatory fire protection assets that must be present.
records.reference: An exception allows part of a taxiing aircraft to pass within the 50-foot hot refueling safety zone, provided its operating engine(s) do not penetrate the 50-foot criteria. During this operation, one flightline fire extinguisher must be located within 100 feet of the aircraft, and one ARFF vehicle must be in standby posture.
records.answer:
Exception for taxiing aircraft within the 50-foot hot refueling zone (TO 00-25-172):

- Engine boundary rule: Part of an aircraft may pass within 50 feet of a hot refueling operation, as long as the operating engine(s) of the taxiing aircraft do not penetrate the 50-foot criteria. The separation shall not be reduced below 50 feet for existing parking areas.
